- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for early positive sentiment.
- After a strong price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistic; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- In low-sentiment periods, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast if recent 10-day average is higher than 30-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment turns positive within next 3 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.2/0.0), model often averages out sentiment; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 50% recent sentiment, 50% historical) to adjust forecast direction.
